en: Therīgāthā 5.9 Pañcakanipāta:
The Verse of the Elder Nun Bhaddā Kuṇḍalakesā
With shorn hair and smeared with mud, wearing but a single robe,
I wandered in the past;
regarding what was blameless as blameworthy, my mind was set on evil.
Perceiving what is blameworthy, she avoided it.
Having emerged from her daytime retreat on Mount Vulture Peak, she went forth.
I saw the stainless Buddha,
honored by the community of monks;
having knelt and paid homage, I—
I placed my hands together in salutation before her;
she said to me, "Come, blessed one," and that was my full ordination.
The Cinas, Aṅgas, Magadhas,
Vajjis, Kāsīs, and Kosalas were free from debt for fifty years.
I did not eat the alms-food of the country.
Truly, he has generated much merit;
truly, this lay follower is wise.
“He who gave the robe to Bhaddā,
who is completely liberated from all fetters.
… Thus spoke the Elder Nun Bhaddā Kuṇḍalakesā.
